newsitem.title: USA: Two blasts rock Atlanta abortion clinic. [CORRECTED 23:32 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Two blasts rock Atlanta abortion clinic. [CORRECTED 23:32 GMT]

text.p: Two explosions rocked a building housing an Atlanta abortion clinic on Thursday, the second injuring several people including emergency officials who had answered the initial call.

The first blast shattered one side of the building housing the Atlanta Northside Family Planning Services centre at around 9:30 a.m. EST (1430 GMT). Police said no one was injured at the site, located in a suburban community known as Sandy Springs.

But a little over an hour later, with emergency workers and TV camera crews milling about the site, a second explosion destroyed a garbage container in a corner of the adjacent parking lot, knocking people to the ground.

Fulton County Police said several people, primarily police and fire officials, were hurt in the second blast. Eyewitnesses said TV camera crews filming the scene also suffered injuries. Local television showed a man described as an agent with the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms being helped from the area.

"There was a big blast. It was almost like someone pushed you as hard as you possibly could be pushed. And all of a sudden it was pandemonium," a photographer who was near the dumpster said on local television.
Police said they suspected that bombs were responsible for both explosions, even though there was no warning.
"It appears to have been some sort of device. It was not a natural explosion," said Fulton County Police Lt. C.C. Cass.
City officials immediately stepped up security at other local abortion clinics.
Local press reports said the same clinic had been the site of a bomb attack in 1984.
The bombing incident was the second serious one within the past six months in Atlanta. (corrects timescale)
On July 27 during the Summer Olympics, a bomb exploded at Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park, leaving two dead and injuring more than 100. No one has been charged in that incident.
The first explosion at the abortion clinic building, which rattled dinner plates in homes miles away, occurred on the third floor -- two stories above the clinic, police said.
But an eyewitness who was working in a third-floor attorney's office at the time told local TV that she believed the explosion had been inside the clinic.
The blast initially started a fire and portions of the building were engulfed in flames and heavy smoke until firefighters brought the blaze under control.
"The structure's standing. There's smoke damage, some windows broken," Cass said.
